title: Effect of the Record Machine
statement: Let $k,n\in\mathbb N$, let $x$ be a finite binary input, and let $d$ be a configuration of a $(k+2)$-work-tape machine with record states, while $c$ is a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine and $a$ is one of its actions. Let $b$ be a Boolean record of width $4k+4$. Suppose $d$ starts in the record machine's initial state, the record tape contains $b$ at each of the next $4k+4$ cells from its head, and $b$ is the prefix of length $4k+4$ of the binary encoding of $a$. Suppose also that $d$ and $c$ have the same input-head position, their first $k$ work tapes and head positions agree, and the summary tape of $d$ currently reads the output summary of $c$. After $4k+5$ steps, the record machine is halted; its input-head position, first $k$ work tapes and their head positions, and summary-tape symbol agree with those obtained by applying $a$ to $c$, while its output list is unchanged from $d$. It does not halt at any earlier time; the encoded action has length at least $4k+5$; and at every time $u\le 4k+5$, the original work-tape heads have moved by their prescribed action displacements only at the final time, every work-tape head has moved by at most $1$ on the first $k$ tapes and at most $4k+4$ on the other two, the input head has moved by at most $1$, the record-tape head has advanced by $\min(u,4k+4)$, and the summary-tape head has not moved.
hypotheses_covered: $d$ starts in the record machine's initial state
the record tape contains $b$ at each offset from the record head
$b$ is the length-$4k+4$ prefix of the encoding of $a$
the first $k$ work-tape head positions agree
the summary tape reads the output summary of $c$
